# Spook (Home Assistant custom integration) misbehaving across repairs, services and helpers — without a test suite

This add-on looks over a smart-home installation, warns about anything in it that points at something no longer there, and adds a handful of extra one-shot calls for tidying that installation up. After an upgrade almost all of that housekeeping reports nonsense, and some of it fails outright. Nothing about the installation itself changed, and in several places a broken behaviour sits directly beside a working one, so please check both sides.

Asking it whether a `prefix.key` name — the kind used to say when a rule fires, or to say what must hold true before it acts — is a real one now gets the verdict wrong in both directions for every case I tried. Ordinary built-in kinds, which have no add-on behind them at all, no longer come back as known. Keys belonging to an add-on that is installed but not currently loaded are treated wrongly as well, and so are keys naming an add-on that ships no such kind and keys naming an add-on that isn't installed at all — those last two should be flagged, and now the answer is unreliable either way. The shortcut that used to look one add-on up a single time for several keys sharing it no longer behaves as it did.
